resources.name: Service
resources.description: Service is a base class for defining the Service hierarchy. All Services are characterized as either being possibly visible and usable by a Customer or not. This gives rise to the two subclasses of Service: CustomerFacingService and ResourceFacingService.

fields.description: Is it a customer facing or resource facing service

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free-text description of the service

fields.name: endDate
fields.description: Date when the service ends

fields.name: hasStarted
fields.description: If TRUE, this Service has already been started

fields.name: isServiceEnabled
fields.description: If FALSE, this particular Service has NOT been enabled for use

fields.name: isStateful
fields.description: If TRUE, this Service can be changed without affecting any other services

fields.name: name
fields.description: Name of the service

fields.name: serviceDate
fields.description: Date when the service was created (whatever its status).

fields.name: serviceType
fields.description: Business type of the service

fields.name: startDate
fields.description: Date when the service starts

fields.description: This attribute is an enumerated integer that indicates how the Service is started, such as: 0: Unknown; 1: Automatically by the managed environment; 2: Automatically by the owning device; 3: Manually by the Provider of the Service; 4: Manually by a Customer of the Provider; 5: Any of the above

fields.description: The life cycle state of the service, such as: feasibilityChecked, designed, reserved, active, inactive, terminated

resources.name: ServiceCatalog
resources.description:
The root entity for service catalog management.
A service catalog is a group of service specifications made available through service candidates that an organization provides to the consumers (internal consumers like its employees or B2B customers or B2C customers). 
A service catalog typically includes name, description and time period that is valid for. It will have a list of ServiceCandidate catalog items. A ServiceCandidate is an entity that makes a ServiceSpecification available to a catalog.
A ServiceCandidate and its associated ServiceSpecification may be "published" - made visible -in any number of ServiceCatalogs, or in none.

resources.name: ServiceProblem
resources.description: The problem information for Middle B which is abstracted in the service layer from the issued event information by First B

fields.name: affectedNumberOfServices
fields.description: Number of affected services

fields.name: category
fields.description: Classifier for the problem. Settable. For example, this is used for distinguish the category of problem originator in [role].[category] format. Example: serviceProvider.declarer, supplier.originated, system.originated

fields.name: correlationId
fields.description: Additional identifier coming from an external system

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free form text describing the Service Problem

fields.name: impactImportanceFactor
fields.description: Impact Importance is characterized by an Impact Importance Factor: overall importance of the impact of all the affected services, e.g. 0 (zero impact) to 100 (worst impact). The Impact Importance is a calculated field which is set by the OSS determining the impact.

fields.name: originatingSystem
fields.description: Indicates where the problem was generated

fields.name: priority
fields.description: An indication varying from 1 (highest) to 10 (lowest) of how important it is for the service provider to correct the Service Problem.

fields.name: problemEscalation
fields.description: Indicates if this service problem has been escalated or not. Possible values are 0 to 10. A value of zero means no escalation. The meanings of values 1-10 are to be determined by the user of the interface, but they show increasing levels of escalation.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: Free text or optionally structured text. It can be Unknown.

fields.name: resolutionDate
fields.description: Time the problem was resolved

fields.name: status
fields.description: The current status of the service problem. Possible values are Submitted, Rejected, Acknowledged, In Progress [Held, Pending], Resolved, Closed, and Cancelled.

fields.name: statusChangeDate
fields.description: Time the problem was last status changed

fields.name: statusChangeReason
fields.description: The reason of state change

fields.name: timeChanged
fields.description: Time the problem was last changed

fields.name: timeRaised
fields.description: Time the problem was raised

flattenedRefs.name: firstAlert
flattenedRefs.description: Indicates what first alerted the system to the problem. It is not the root cause of the Service Problem. Examples: Threshold crossing alert

flattenedRefs.name: impactPatterns
flattenedRefs.description: Define the patterns of impact (optional)- e.g. other service characteristics- Used when defining impact through another pattern than the predefined attributes.

flattenedRefs.name: originatorParty
flattenedRefs.description: Individual or organization that created the problem

resources.name: ServiceSpecification
resources.description:
ServiceSpecification is a class that offers characteristics to describe a type of service.
Functionally, it acts as a template by which Services may be instantiated. By sharing the same  specification, these services would therefore share the same set of characteristics.

fields.name: description
fields.description: A narrative that explains in detail what the serviceSpecCharacteristic is

fields.name: extensible
fields.description: An indicator that specifies that the values for the characteristic can be extended by adding new values when instantiating a characteristic for an Entity.

fields.name: isUnique
fields.description: An indicator that specifies if a value is unique for the specification. Possible values are; "unique while value is in effect" and "unique whether value is in effect or not"

In general, a determinate quantity or magnitude of the kind designated, taken as a standard of comparison for others of the same kind, in assigning to them numerical values, as 1 foot, 1 yard, 1 mile, 1 square foot.

fields.name: conformanceTargetLower
fields.description:

resources.name: UsageConsumptionReport
resources.description: An usage consumption report enables to know at a given point the balances and the consumption counters related to various buckets (SMS, Voice, Data for example). It could be calculated for a device identified by a public key (msisdn number for a mobile device for example or PSTN or VOIP number for a fix device), for a subscribed offer or option or for an user.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Free short text describing the usage consumption report content

fields.name: effectiveDate
fields.description: Date and time when the usage consumption report was calculated and generated

fields.name: name
fields.description: Usage consumption report name

subResources.description: Bucket(s) included in the offer or option subscribed.

fields.name: isShared
fields.description: True if the bucket is shared between several devices or users

fields.name: name
fields.description: Bucket name

fields.name: usageType
fields.description: Type of usage concerned by the bucket, such as voice, sms, data

children.description: The balance (called UsageVolumeBalance in the SID model) defines the remaining allowed product usage quantity in terms of volume, time, currency or events. It corresponds to the initial allowed usage quantity minus the usage consumed on the bucket.

fields.name: remainingValueName
fields.description: Remaining value in a formatted string for the bucket given in the balance unit (for example 1.9 Gb). This formatted string could be used for display needs for example

flattenedRefs.name: remainingValue
flattenedRefs.description: Numeric remaining value for the bucket given in the unit (for example 1.9). This numeric value could be used for calculation for example

flattenedRefs.name: validFor
flattenedRefs.description: Balance period between a start date time and an end date time. For prepaid bucket, the period of the balance is between the  effective date of the usage consumption report generation and the end date of the bucket. For postpaid bucket, the period of the balance is between the effective date of the usage consumption report generation and the next bill date.

children.description: The consumption counters (called ConsumptionSummary in the SID model) detail for example the different kind of consumption done on the bucket.

fields.name: counterType
fields.description: Type of the consumption counter. We can give for example a counter of the used value for a bucket (counterType=used for example) or the value of the consumption done out of the bucket(s) (counterType=outOfBucket for example)

fields.name: level
fields.description: Counter level. The counter can be given globally for the bucket or detailed by user or by network product for example in case of shared bucket

fields.name: valueName
fields.description: Value of the counter in a formatted string used for display needs for example

flattenedRefs.name: consumptionPeriod
flattenedRefs.description: Consumption counter period between a start date time and an end date time. For prepaid bucket, the period of counters is between the start date of the bucket and the effective date of the usage consumption report generation. For postpaid bucket, the period of counters is between the last bill date and the effective date of the usage consumption report generation.

flattenedRefs.name: product
flattenedRefs.description: Public identifier associated to the product for which the consumption counter is detailed. If the level of the counter is global (i.e. concerning all the network products), the list of them is not specified. It can be found through the network products listed in the bucket sub-resource

flattenedRefs.name: user
flattenedRefs.description: Reference of the user for which the consumption counter is detailed. If the level of the counter is global (i.e. concerning all the users), the list of them is not specified. It can be found through the users listed in the network products of the bucket sub-resource

flattenedRefs.name: value
flattenedRefs.description: Numeric value of the bucket counter in a given unit

children.description: An instantiated network product (specialization of a product) subscribed by a customer.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Network product name

fields.name: publicIdentifier
fields.description: Public number associated to the network product (msisdn number for mobile line for example)
